A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with indiSplit renamed scSplit. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original microscopy unmixing experiments, component analyses, and a GoPro deblurring experiment in Supplementary Section S.7.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds normalization controls, mixing-mismatch tests, and downstream segmentation results.

M1.justification: The proposed generators, mixing-ratio regressor, severity-specific normalization, aggregation, losses, and sampling distribution are retained. Appendix D expands inference documentation and states that one-step inference was always used; it does not establish a changed experimental method.

E1.justification: The five microscopy datasets and channel-pair tasks, together with GoPro deblurring, remain. Coverage expands within these datasets through downstream BioSR segmentation and explicit HTT24 training/test mixing-mismatch scenarios.

E2.justification: MicroSplit, discussed but not evaluated in v1, joins both main comparison tables. Supplementary Table S.1 additionally evaluates first-layer and all-layer instance-normalization variants of InDI and scSplit, substantially extending comparisons relevant to the normalization contribution.

E3.justification: New protocols quadruple either HTT24 training channel before evaluating unchanged raw test images. The BioSR segmentation experiment trains 24 FeatureForest models across four methods, two channels, and three mixing ratios, using manual annotations and Dice dissimilarity. These are additional evaluation designs, not revisions to the retained benchmark settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds full-model SCIN removal across four datasets, instance-normalization controls on Hagen and PaviaATN, and real-image robustness tests under training/test mixing mismatch. These substantially extend v1's retained regressor, aggregation, augmentation, and precision analyses.

E5.justification: Supplementary Tables S.9 and S.10 newly report standard errors across test frames for the main benchmark results. This adds broad uncertainty reporting beyond v1. The existing averaging of ten predictions remains unchanged; additional training runs or seeds are not established.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Tables 1 and 2 are unchanged. V2 adds MicroSplit scores, normalization-control results, segmentation results, and raw-image examples. For example, new Table 3 reports 35.8 dB for scSplit versus 30.1 for U-Net and 28.8 for denoiSplit under HTT24(4:1); this is a new-setting comparison, not a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation 9 in Appendix A replaces v1's unaveraged channel-variance terms with their expectations in the expected-variance identity. This is a limited mathematical revision. The image-level derivation and underlying assumptions otherwise remain substantially the same.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: severity-aware mixing-ratio estimation and normalization enable fluorescence image splitting and bleedthrough removal across five public datasets. The new experiments support this contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive arguments about SCIN preserving intensity cues compared with instance normalization, the fidelity rationale for one-step inference, and choosing 100 normalization intervals without claiming universal optimality. It also adds an interference-based imaging limitation and emphasizes tolerance to small regressor errors when interpreting the retained analysis.

D1.justification: V2 supplements existing implementation details with explicit one-step inference, 450K iterations, batch size eight, four workers, hardware and timing information, and FeatureForest settings. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing settings. V1's promised permissive source release is removed without replacement access information.

R1.justification: The existing microscopy and InDI positioning is largely retained. Four references are added: FeatureForest, two works supporting the instance-normalization discussion, and the perception-distortion tradeoff. These provide focused support for the new evaluation and interpretation.

P1.justification: V2 renames the method, introduces the SCIN acronym, and locally rewrites normalization, results, and conclusion passages while retaining the main narrative order. Appendix headings are reorganized, but several references become stale: Section 4 directs readers to Appendix B for evaluation methodology, which is actually Appendix E.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation with widespread display resizing and relocation. The framework schematic is revised, the opening illustration moves to the supplement, and Figure 3 loses a panel retained elsewhere. New result, ablation, uncertainty tables, and raw-image figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation gaps through direct SCIN and instance-normalization controls, real-image mixing-mismatch tests, and downstream segmentation results. Newly reported frame-based standard errors make the core comparisons easier to assess. Together these substantially strengthen scrutiny of the normalization contribution and practical utility. The gains outweigh the modest drawbacks of removing the source-release promise and introducing stale appendix references.
